text: Donald Andrew McClurkin Jr. (born November 9, 1959) is an American gospel singer and minister who has won three Grammy Awards, ten Stellar Awards, two BET Awards, two Soul Train Awards, one Dove Award, and one NAACP Image Award. He is one of the top-selling gospel artists, having sold over 13 million albums. Variety referred to him as a "Reigning King of Urban Gospel." McClurkin was born in Copiague, New York. At age eight, his two-year-old brother was killed by a speeding driver, causing family turmoil. He later experienced childhood sexual abuse from his great uncle and his great uncle's son. Two of his sisters struggled with substance abuse, prompting McClurkin to find solace in church and through an aunt who sang background vocals with gospel musician Andraé Crouch. By adolescence, he formed the McClurkin Singers and later the New York Restoration Choir, releasing recordings as early as 1975. He released three albums with the choir before launching a solo career. In 1989, he was hired as an associate minister at Marvin Winans' Perfecting Church in Detroit, Michigan, serving as an assistant for over a decade. In 1991, McClurkin was diagnosed with leukemia after experiencing sharp pain, swelling, and internal bleeding; at age 31, he chose to follow his own advice to "believe that God will save you" and practice what he preached. In 2001, he was ordained and sent by Marvin Winans to establish Perfecting Faith Church in Freeport, New York, where he serves as senior pastor. A friendship with a Warner Alliance executive led to his signing with the label for his 1996 self-titled album, produced by Bill Maxwell, Mark Kibble of Take 6, Cedric and Victor Caldwell, and Andraé Crouch. The album, featuring the popular song "Stand," went gold after being praised by Oprah Winfrey. At the 48th Annual Grammy Awards, he won Best Traditional Soul Gospel Album for "Psalms, Hymns & Spiritual Songs." McClurkin is best known for his hit songs "Stand" and "We Fall Down," which were played extensively on Gospel and Urban radio. His three solo albums have topped the Billboard Charts. Following the success of his near double platinum album "Live in London and More," he released "Psalms, Hymns and Spiritual Songs" in 2005 and "We All Are One: Live In Detroit" in 2009, both of which topped Billboard charts across genres. In 2014, he released "Duets," featuring artists such as Mary Mary’s Erica and Tina Campbell, Fred Hammond, John P. Kee, Dorinda Clark-Cole, Tramaine Hawkins, Israel Houghton, and Tye Tribbett. The album debuted at No. 45 on the Billboard 200 and No. 4 on the Gospel Billboard charts. His 2016 album "The Journey" debuted at number one on the Billboard Top Gospel Albums chart, marking his seventh solo release and including live performances of classics like "Speak to My Heart," "Great Is Your Mercy," "Stand," and "That’s What I Believe." His last recorded album, "A Different Song," was released in 2019 and debuted at No. 2 on the Gospel Billboard charts. McClurkin includes a language medley—Japanese, Russian, Spanish, and Dutch—in most live performances due to his love for sharing gospel music globally. Tom Versen and Tony Sisti of T&T Creative signed him to a radio syndication deal with Dial Global Local and syndicator Gary Bernstein, providing a mobile recording studio based in his church for on-the-road broadcasts. He stated, "As much as I love music and singing, I really love doing radio and the direct feedback I get from my listeners all over the country. I never thought I would be having this much fun doing radio, and I could touch and impact so many beautiful people." In 2009, he launched the television series *Perfecting Your Faith* on cable. His television appearances include *Good Morning America*, CBS’s *The Early Show*, *The View*, *Girlfriends*, and *The Parkers*. He has also appeared in films such as *The Gospel* and *The Fighting Temptations*, playing a single man or a church pastor. In 2002, McClurkin told a Christian website that due to sexual abuse and exposure to pornography, he had struggled with homosexuality, stating he "turned" gay as a result of childhood molestation and traumatic pornography exposure but was able to reverse his orientation through "will and prayer." He later said he had rejected that "lifestyle," asserting, "I’ve been through this and have experienced God’s power to change my lifestyle. I am delivered, and I know God can deliver others, too." His inclusion as a headlining performer for Senator Barack Obama’s 2008 presidential campaign sparked controversy due to his views on homosexuality, leading to his removal from the performance roster, though he still performed at one concert. In August 2013, he was disinvited from the 50th anniversary of the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom due to his ex-gay status being seen as disruptive. In 2015, he spoke out against same-sex marriage following the U.S. Supreme Court’s legalization of it nationwide. McClurkin has a son, Matthew, born in 2000. He is also related to singer Marsha McClurkin of the short-lived new jack swing group Abstrac. In 2018, McClurkin survived a serious road accident after losing consciousness while driving. In January 2026, McClurkin was sued for sexual assault by Giuseppe Corletto, a former personal assistant from 2004 to 2008. The lawsuit, filed in the Manhattan Supreme Court, claims Corletto met McClurkin in 2003 after reading his autobiography, which described his deliverance from homosexuality. Corletto became McClurkin’s assistant in 2004, and within two years, the lawsuit alleges McClurkin began grope him during "pray the gay away" sessions. The abuse is said to have occurred at Perfecting Faith Church and during work trips over several years. After an alleged assault in 2013, McClurkin allegedly wrote an email apologizing for his actions, referring to himself as a "dirty old man." McClurkin’s attorney responded that the allegations are "categorically false." The BET Awards are awarded annually by Black Entertainment Television; McClurkin has received two awards from five nominations. The Dove Awards are awarded annually by the Gospel Music Association; he has won four awards from thirteen nominations. The Grammy Awards are awarded annually by the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences; McClurkin has won three awards from five nominations. The Soul Train Music Awards are awarded annually; he has received two awards from five nominations. The Stellar Awards are awarded annually by SAGMA; McClurkin has received twelve awards from twenty-four nominations.
